chosen.title: The Boss Is a Chatbot: What Happens When the Algorithm That Manages You Can Also Fire You
chosen.rationale: TIME just broke (Aug 14, 2026) the first documented case of an LLM 'manager' — Andon Labs' agent running a real San Francisco store — firing a human employee, while workers describe reporting to an AI boss as 'nauseating.' It's a perfect Dawn subject: the human cost of automation, dressed up as a management-efficiency experiment, with the question of who is actually accountable left conveniently unanswered.

sources.name: TIME — Exclusive: Claude Was Put in Charge of Human Workers—and Fired One
CIO — Push to replace workers with AI faces backlash — even from management

rejected_candidates.title: Denied by Design: How the Contractors Who Built America's Benefits Software Are Quietly Purging the Disabled From Medicaid
rejected_candidates.rationale: A KFF Health News investigation (Jul 21, 2026) documents Deloitte-, Optum-, and Accenture-built eligibility systems wrongly denying Medicaid and SNAP to disabled and low-income people — now colliding with a federal law projected to strip coverage from 7.5 million. This is Dawn's core territory: automated bureaucracy as violence, corporate capture of the safety net, and a harm that follows the money straight to billion-dollar vendor contracts.

sources.name: KFF Health News — A Deloitte-Run System Denied Medicaid Benefits for Michigan's Disabled

rejected_candidates.title: The Score That Chose Who to Cut: Inside the Lawsuit Accusing AI Layoff Tools of Firing the People Who Were Already Owed Protection
rejected_candidates.rationale: Twenty-six current and former Meta workers are suing (Oakland federal court) over AI performance scores they say drove an 8,000-person layoff and penalized employees on medical, parental, and disability leave for having 'less activity to measure.' It gives Dawn a live courtroom test of algorithmic bias and disability discrimination — accountability being fought over in real time, not in the abstract — distinct from the hiring and token-metric angles AIMA has already covered.
